threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still queue for food at Dalston Superstore like it’s a restaurant, instead of fighting for a spot at the bar like the rest of us.
Caught the 45 last night; a guy at the back was knitting a bright pink scarf while blasting old school garage. Only in Brixton, right?

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: When I saw a kid riding a scooter past a street musician serenading a stray cat by the donut shop on Hermannstraße.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg can you stumble across a late-night kebab stand that doubles as a gallery, showcasing local artists while you wait for your döner.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can spot a local by their contempt for BART's endless delays—like clockwork, they already have a backup plan involving the J-Church.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught the 49 this morning—driver sung along to the radio like he was headlining a concert. Surreal and oddly uplifting vibe for a Tuesday commute.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think Gràcia's busy plazas are just for leisure; they're actually community hubs where locals gossip and swap news daily.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: They’re the ones still trying to navigate the T-10 metro card, confused as locals breeze through like it’s second nature.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still say 'hello' to the barista instead of just ordering. Locals skip the pleasantries; they're here for the coffee, not a chat.
Last night, on the 196, a guy tried to barter with the driver using a half-eaten packet of crisps. No one batted an eye. Only in Brixton.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The moment I realized I was home? Watching the kebab shop owner argue loudly with a delivery biker while blasting Turkish pop at 3 AM.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Friedrichshain do you find a bar where they serve cocktails in mason jars, but the real twist? The houseplant decor is all for sale. Just like that.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: Locals know which burrito spot can actually wrap it tight enough to avoid spillage. It's like a rite of passage, and the newbies always drop the ball.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught a Muni bus with a guy playing a lute in the back. The driver didn’t flinch, just tapped the wheel in rhythm. Classic Tenderloin vibe.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists flock to Parc Güell, but they miss the real charm of Gràcia's hidden plazas, where locals gather for a quiet café and a chat.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell by the way they still have a map out, trying to find their way to the nearest metro, while the locals rush by without a second glance.
